classification.difficultyReason: Factorise several quadratics, convert division to multiplication by a reciprocal, and cancel common factors, including a reversed-sign factor.

answer.worked:
Factorise the numerators and denominators:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2+4x+3}{x^2+x-6}\times\frac{x^2-4}{x^2+5x+4}&=\frac{(x+1)(x+3)}{(x+3)(x-2)}\times\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{(x+1)(x+4)}\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the common factors:
$$\frac{(x+1)(x+3)(x-2)(x+2)}{(x+3)(x-2)(x+1)(x+4)}=\frac{x+2}{x+4}.$$

For the non-monic denominator, split the middle term:
$$\begin{aligned}2x^2-5x-3&=2x^2-6x+x-3\\2x^2-5x-3&=2x(x-3)+(x-3)\\2x^2-5x-3&=(2x+1)(x-3).\end{aligned}$$
Factorise the other quadratics and cancel common factors:
$$\frac{(x+1)(x+6)}{(x+2)(x-1)}\times\frac{(x-3)(x+2)}{(2x+1)(x-3)}=\frac{(x+1)(x+6)}{(x-1)(2x+1)}.$$

Factorise and multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction:
$$\frac{x^2+3x-4}{x^2+4x}\div\frac{x^2+x-2}{x+2}=\frac{(x+4)(x-1)}{x(x+4)}\times\frac{x+2}{(x+2)(x-1)}.$$
Cancel the common factors:
$$\frac{(x+4)(x-1)(x+2)}{x(x+4)(x+2)(x-1)}=\frac{1}{x}.$$

Split the middle terms to factorise the denominators:
$$\begin{aligned}2x^2+3x+1&=2x(x+1)+(x+1)\\2x^2+3x+1&=(2x+1)(x+1)\\2x^2+7x+3&=2x(x+3)+(x+3)\\2x^2+7x+3&=(2x+1)(x+3).\end{aligned}$$
Use $9-9x=-9(x-1)$ and multiply by the reciprocal:
$$\frac{3x(x-1)}{(2x+1)(x+1)}\times\frac{(2x+1)(x+3)}{-9(x-1)}=-\frac{x(x+3)}{3(x+1)}.$$
